description: Swarm node and container resource pressure using existing sysmetrics node-exporter jobs and cAdvisor. CPU, memory, disk, I/O-wait, load per core and container CPU throttling; no Kubernetes or new collectors.

options.content:
# PCA Swarm Resource Health

Existing node-exporter and cAdvisor metrics show CPU, memory, disk, I/O-wait, load per core and container CPU throttling. Start with the cluster overview, find busy nodes, then inspect heavy containers.

**Filters:** `node` selects node-exporter instances in per-node panels. Cluster gauges always cover all reporting nodes. `cadvisorHost` and `container` select container metrics independently: cloud node-exporter instances use VM names, whereas cAdvisor instances use target addresses. Container legends include the cAdvisor instance to distinguish hosts.

**Not collected:** desired/running Swarm replicas, application readiness, restart counts, OOM termination reasons, resource requests and per-volume disk usage. Filesystem panels show host storage, not volume attribution. Missing cAdvisor task metrics are not zero usage.

panels.description: Average CPU used across all nodes (1 - idle). Orange >=80%, red >=90% – the cluster is CPU-bound; find the hot node(s) in Per-node.
panels.title: Cluster CPU utilisation

panels.description: Used memory across all nodes (1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal). Orange >=85%, red >=95% – risk of OOM kills and swapping/sluggishness.
panels.title: Cluster memory utilisation

panels.description: Highest filesystem usage on any node/mount. Orange >=80%, red >=90% – a full disk stalls writes (HDFS/MinIO/Postgres/Kafka) and can crash services.
panels.title: Fullest filesystem

panels.description: Average CPU time waiting on disk I/O across nodes. Orange >=5%, red >=10% – the disk subsystem is the bottleneck; CPU is idle waiting for storage.
panels.title: Cluster I/O-wait

panels.description: Total 1-min load average / total logical cores. Orange >=1, red >=2 – more runnable work than CPUs = queuing/slowness.
panels.title: Load per core (cluster)

panels.description: Number of nodes reporting node-exporter metrics in this cluster.
panels.title: Nodes

panels.description: The busiest nodes by CPU right now. Orange ≥ 80%, red ≥ 90% – a node near 100% will throttle/queue its containers; check the Top containers CPU panel to see which containers are driving it, or reschedule/scale.
panels.title: Top nodes – CPU utilisation %

panels.description: The fullest nodes by memory right now. Orange ≥ 80%, red ≥ 90% – a node near 100% risks kernel OOM-kills of its containers; identify heavy containers (Top containers memory) or add capacity.
panels.title: Top nodes – memory utilisation %

panels.description: Absolute CPU cores consumed per node right now. Compare against each node's core count to spot imbalance across the cluster. Not threshold-coloured (core counts differ by node).
panels.title: Top nodes – CPU cores used

panels.description: Absolute memory used per node right now (total − available). Use with memory % to see both pressure and raw footprint. Not threshold-coloured (node sizes differ).
panels.title: Top nodes – memory used

panels.description: Nodes spending the most CPU time waiting on disk. Orange ≥ 10%, red ≥ 25% – high I/O-wait means storage is the bottleneck; see the disk I/O utilisation panel and the Host Filesystems row.
panels.title: Top nodes – I/O-wait %

panels.description: Run-queue pressure normalised by core count (load1 / cores). Orange ≥ 1 (fully committed), red ≥ 2 (over-subscribed) – sustained > 1 means processes are waiting for CPU on that node.
panels.title: Top nodes – load per core

panels.description: Per-node CPU used (1 - idle). Dashed lines mark the 80%/90% thresholds. A node pinned near/over the red line is CPU-bound – drill into Per-container to see which containers on it are heaviest.
panels.title: Node – CPU utilisation %

panels.description: Per-node memory utilisation (1 - MemAvailable/MemTotal). High usage risks memory pressure; inspect container working sets. OOM termination reasons are not collected.
panels.title: Node – memory utilisation %

panels.description: Per-node CPU time spent waiting on disk I/O. Thresholds 5%/10%. Sustained high I/O-wait = the node's disks cannot keep up; correlate with Disk IO % below and the storage containers (HDFS/MinIO/Kafka/Postgres).
panels.title: Node – I/O-wait %

panels.description: Per-node 1-min load average divided by that node's logical cores. Thresholds 1/2. > 1 per core = more runnable work than CPUs (queuing). Compare with CPU% – high load with moderate CPU often means I/O-wait. (Fixed: load1 is summed by instance so it matches the per-node core count.)
panels.title: Node – load average per core

panels.description: Per-node, per-mount filesystem usage. Thresholds 80%/90%. A mount near red will stop accepting writes – identify the node/mount and free space or expand the volume.
panels.title: Node – filesystem usage % (by mount)

panels.description: Fraction of time each disk device was busy (node_disk_io_time_seconds_total rate). ~100% = the device is saturated and is the bottleneck behind high I/O-wait. Correlate with the storage services on that node.
panels.title: Node – disk I/O utilisation % (by device)

panels.description: Existing cAdvisor task metrics, grouped by host and container name. CPU is in cores; memory is the working set; throttling is the percentage of CFS periods throttled (only when periods are reported). Missing task metrics indicate unavailable telemetry, not zero usage.
panels.title: Top containers - CPU (cores)

panels.description: Existing cAdvisor task metrics, grouped by host and container name. CPU is in cores; memory is the working set; throttling is the percentage of CFS periods throttled (only when periods are reported). Missing task metrics indicate unavailable telemetry, not zero usage.
panels.title: Top containers - memory

panels.description: Existing cAdvisor task metrics, grouped by host and container name. CPU is in cores; memory is the working set; throttling is the percentage of CFS periods throttled (only when periods are reported). Missing task metrics indicate unavailable telemetry, not zero usage.
panels.title: Top containers - CPU throttling %

panels.description: Fullest host filesystems by node and mount. This does not measure individual Docker volumes.
panels.title: Top nodes – filesystem usage % (node-local disk)
